subject: Enablement sprint & staggered rollout phases — decision input
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <epark@acme-data.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Enablement sprint & staggered rollout phases — decision input

Team —

We're coming up on the planned public beta for the runtime changes (targeting Feb 29). Before we lock the final dates I need alignment on three cross-functional asks so we can 1) publish a clear enablement plan, 2) confirm the rollout gating matrix, and 3) identify any exceptions that require a slower/canary-first approach.

Quick asks:
- Rollout cadence: Can Engineering support a 3‑phase stagger (10% → 50% → 100%) across two weeks, or do we need different timing?
- Docs/enablement: What minimum deliverables do you need from Product (slides, runbooks, playbooks)? I attached a draft enablement outline for context (enablement-outline_v2.pdf).
- CS & partners: What training windows and comms do you need to support a 10% canary?

If we don't converge by EOD Monday (Feb 13) I will propose the fallback: push public beta to Mar 7 and run a single-week canary. Please call out any blockers.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Berger <markus@cloud-partners.io>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enablement sprint & staggered rollout phases — decision input

Marissa —

Short answer: we can support a phased rollout but with constraints. Notes below and a proposed rollout matrix attached (rollout-matrix.xlsx):

Engineering constraints / recommendations:
- Phase length: 3 phases across two weeks is aggressive if any of the following are true: non-trivial schema changes, new quantized runtime variants, or new compilation paths. Recommend 3 phases stretched over 3 weeks (10% → 30% → 100%).
- Gate metrics: target error-rate < 0.5% for 10k requests, median RT < 220ms for host tier A, and token-level quality regression < 1.5% (per RLW-457 eval set).
- Fallbacks: automatic rollback to previous model variant + traffic split to legacy cluster if we see sustained errors > 0.8% over 15m. Need a short runbook for ops and on-call handoff.
- Capacity: for the canary we need reserved burst capacity (one extra DGX pool) for 48 hours in case of rollbacks; that requires approval from infra (we can spin this up but it adds cost).

Open questions for Product/CS:
- Which customers are in the 10% cohort? If partners like Acme Data want early access, we can include them but they must sign the exception SLA.
- Do we want a soft launch (no billing change) or full public beta? Billing changes complicate rollback.

I attached the rollout matrix with gating thresholds and owner columns. Happy to sync on a 30m call Monday.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Engineering, Runtime

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <epark@acme-data.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enablement sprint & staggered rollout phases — decision input

Thanks — good discussion. From CS perspective:

Training & enablement needs:
- Customer-facing playbook (1 pager) + troubleshooting FAQ for first-response teams (we can re-use parts of your runbook).
- Two live training sessions for early-adopter customers (we need two 60min windows: propose Mar 1 and Mar 8).
- Internal enablement: two 45min brown-bag sessions for Support & Solutions Engineers during the week before canary.

Cohort selection: We strongly prefer a mix of partners + low-risk self-serve customers. Elena (Acme Data) is willing to be in the first cohort but they need an explicit rollback SLA and a single technical point-of-contact.

Comms: we need at least 48 hours notice for the canary to schedule CS coverage. If we move to Mar 7 fallback, training windows need to slide accordingly.

Attachment: training-slots.ics (draft times for brown-bags)

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enablement sprint & staggered rollout phases — decision input (summary & next steps)

Folks —

Thanks for the quick turn. Summarizing decisions, owners, and near-term actions so we have a single source of truth:

Decisions:
- Rollout cadence: 3 phases over 3 weeks (10% → 30% → 100%). Final public beta date: Mar 1 (soft launch for partners), full public rollout by Mar 21, pending gates.
- Gates & metrics: follow Vivek's matrix (see RLW-457). Primary gates: error-rate, median RT, and token-level regression thresholds.
- Cohort: partners + vetted low-risk self-serve customers. Acme Data confirmed for 10% cohort (Elena listed here).

Owners & deliverables (owner — due date):
- Product (Marissa) — final enablement deck + 1p playbook, due Feb 20. See draft: enablement-outline_v2.pdf.
- Engineering (Vivek) — finalize rollout matrix & ops runbook, due Feb 22. See attachment rollout-matrix.xlsx. Infra to provision burst capacity for canary window (48h) — cost approval required.
- CS (Grace) — schedule customer training + internal brown-bags; confirm two slots Mar 1 & Mar 8 or slide to Mar 7 & Mar 14 if we take fallback. Training slots draft attached (training-slots.ics).
- Partnerships (Markus) — notify marketplace partners of canary and provide partner-facing notes; coordinate any partner-specific opt-ins.

Open items (action owners):
- Cost approval for burst capacity (Finance/Infra) — Vivek to open cost request (RLW-512).
- Exception SLA for Acme Data — Marissa + Legal to draft by Feb 18.
- Short ops runbook + on-call handoff doc — Vivek to add to Confluence (link below) by Feb 22.

Links & artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=doc-abc123 | Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Enablement+Plan | JIRA: RLW-457, RLW-512

If there are no objections I'll treat these as the agreed plan and start coordinating calendar invites and a single executive update on Feb 23. Please reply with explicit "ack" or call out objections by EOD Feb 17.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Launch Programs & Enablement
Redwood Inference
